what_happened: Dispatch text states meta-builder-agent.md's Stage 1 'has no resolution step of its own to correct' and frames remedy (b) as adding a new resolution step, and separately calls the agent's existing behavior a 'silent cwd fallback'. Git history shows Stage 1 already carries a Defensive fallback (added same-day as skill-meta's own gap acknowledgment, well before both the 2026-10-11 and 2026-11-05 diagnosis dates) that resolves $TARGET_ROOT via ${CLAUDE_AGENT_GLOBAL_ROOT:-$HOME/.config/nvim} and explicitly forbids CWD as a fallback. The real gap is not absence of a resolution step but its unenforced, silent, prose-only compliance -- the Nov-5 recurrence happened despite this fallback already being written.

Enumerated every direct meta-builder-agent dispatcher via two differently-shaped greps (broad text mention, then literal subagent_type token) and found exactly 3 call sites: skill-meta/SKILL.md (correct), context/patterns/telemetry-meta-submode.md (correct), context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md Step 4b (broken, no target_root). Confirms the dispatch's own claim that remedy (a) alone would have sufficed for the measured Nov-5 instance.
